payload.title: Deliver the Printer serverless PDF rendering service on AWS

node.description: A caller sends one job to the SQS queue and receives one result on the chosen callback.
Local development reproduces queue, storage, and callback behaviour with LocalStack.
Job and result contracts are versioned JSON Schemas with generated TypeScript types.
A deployed worker turns a valid dummy job into a stored PDF and an SQS success result.
Retries, DLQ, deterministic print identifiers, and failure results are tested.
Releases are cut by semantic-release and deployed through GitHub OIDC without static keys.
Prints are encrypted, publicly inaccessible, and expire automatically after one day.
All AWS resources are provisioned by Terraform from bootstrap and the printer module.
Conventional Commits, squash merges, and protected main are enforced locally and in CI.
The worker consumes only the jobs queue and may send results only to allowed targets.
Pull requests validate code, contracts, templates, and Terraform before merge.
A deployed smoke test verifies each release, and rollback deploys an earlier release.

payload.note: Approved by the user after reviewing intent/prd.md and intent/trd.md

node.description: One valid job yields exactly one success result.
The submitted refId is echoed unchanged in the result.
A valid job fixture passes the published schema and generated type.
A job without templateId fails schema validation before processing.
A valid _smoke job stores a PDF and returns a success result.
An unknown template returns TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND without retrying.
A retryable failure is retried until the receive count is exhausted, then dead-lettered.
The last allowed attempt delivers a failure result and deletes the job.
Prints expire after one day and presigned links expire after the configured TTL.
Only allowed sender accounts, principals or organization may enqueue jobs.
The worker cannot deliver to a callback target outside the allowed ARNs.
A release commit deploys through GitHub OIDC with a SemVer release.
A non-release commit deploys a sha-<short> release without a tag.
The post-deploy smoke job returns a success result within 60 seconds.
A dispatched rollback deploys an earlier release and passes the smoke test.
Bootstrap creates the state bucket, artifacts bucket, OIDC provider and roles.
The printer module creates the queue, bucket, KMS key, worker and alias.
A valid pull request passes code, contract, LocalStack and Terraform checks.
An invalid contract or Terraform error blocks the pull request.
Commitlint rejects a commit message outside Conventional Commits.
Squash merge puts one conventional commit on main without a merge commit.
A local job stores a PDF in LocalStack and records a success in the sink.
A local unknown-template job records a TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND in the sink.
The operator supplies the GitHub owner and repository name before the first deploy.
The operator supplies the AWS account and region before bootstrap; default is eu-central-1.
An administrator applies bootstrap once before enabling the release workflow.
A deterministic placeholder PDF is acceptable for the Phase 1 exit; Chromium rendering is Phase 3.

payload.note: Discovery complete; all 12 requirements have scenarios and Q-001 items are recorded as assumptions A-001..A-004

node.description: JSON Schema 2020-12 is the public contract; Ajv validates and TypeScript types are generated.
Foundation uses AWS SDK v3, Ajv, uuid, pnpm, Vitest, esbuild and semantic-release.
Phase 1 uses a placeholder PDF renderer and SQS-only result delivery; other channels fail explicitly.
Bootstrap uses local state once; the main deployment uses S3 backend with native locking.
A minimal _smoke template and manifest script prove resolution; full template tooling is Phase 2.
_smoke is the single reserved internal slug, exempt from the public slug pattern.

payload.note: User approved the assessment with 'Ok let's move on'; includes ADR-006 reserved _smoke slug and PDF/A rejection in Phase 1
Plan approved by the user with 'approve'

node.description: Validates inbound print jobs against the JSON Schema contract before domain mapping.
Validates outbound results against the JSON Schema contract, including error codes and metadata.
Orchestrates one print job through template resolution, rendering, storage and result delivery.
Base domain error carrying a public error code and retryability for every print failure.
Lambda SQS entry point that validates records, processes jobs and reports batch item failures.
Single composition root wiring config, manifest, AWS clients, adapters and the print use case.
Stores one PDF under prints/<printId>.pdf with SHA-256, size and a presigned GET.
Delivers success or failure results to an SQS queue, including FIFO identifiers.
Resolves template ids and slugs from the bundled, content-hashed manifest.
Phase 1 deterministic placeholder PDF producer behind the renderer port.
Derives deterministic UUIDv5 print ids from inbound SQS message ids.
Builds the release-aware template manifest with sorted SHA-256 content hashes.

payload.title: Complete the Printer service with templates, rendering, callbacks and production readiness

node.description: Handlebars template engine supports lenient, strict and assume-objects modes with a fixed helper set.
The manifest records placeholders extracted from the Handlebars AST for every template.
Template CLI commands create, validate, check and preview templates and build the manifest.
A real annual-statement template renders by id and slug after deploy, plain and PDF/A.
Template validation rejects invalid identity, compilation and sample data; check blocks id/slug changes.
The optional network module supports VPC create and lookup with endpoints and optional NAT.
Chromium renders templates with JavaScript disabled, request interception and the specified page settings.
PDF/A post-processing produces all eight levels with sRGB ICC, XMP and required safety checks.
All five result channels and ping deliver end to end with the documented failure handling.
HTTP callbacks enforce the allowlist plus DNS and link-local/metadata SSRF checks.
CI render regression compares page count, text and appearance for plain and PDF/A PDFs.
A throughput target is agreed and verified with Power Tuning and a load test.
Opt-in alarms and a runbook cover rollback, DLQ redrive, template removal and recovery.
Plain and PDF/A smoke jobs verify each release and the first real template is live.
Bootstrap, OIDC deploy, branch protection and rollback are verified in the real AWS account.
